queue_items.claim: The rejection of the merger rival is argued only from this side of the closing seam and never weighs the cross-seam catchword the row itself discloses, which argues continuity across the very seam the rival attacks.
queue_items.grounds: The row's closing seam is 1:3|1:4. device_notes discloses a catchword straddling it: בָּנִים֙ (oshb:Isa.1.2, token 8 of 13) against בָּנִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.1.4, token 9 of 19); the two carry different cantillation, so byte tier fails and the pair collates at accent_stripped tier exactly as the row names it, and the count object is right - the bare plural noun stands at 8 verses book-wide token-exact on re-sweep (sweep: 8 verses, skeleton, token-exact), where the naive contiguous-substring object returns 14 verses. The rejection field answers the rival from the summons imperatives שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ (oshb:Isa.1.2, tokens 1-4, byte tier, re-collated) plus an asserted distinctness of speech-move; the far side's own bytes - the verse-initial ה֣וֹי (oshb:Isa.1.4, token 1, byte tier), which boundary_rationale does name as the seam signal - are never cited in the rejection, and the disclosed catchword is never weighed against the merger. The seam is not thereby shown wrong: the hoy onset is a ruled tier-1 signal standing in 1:4's own bytes, the cross-seam disclosure obligation is met in device_notes, and no tier-4 signal appears anywhere in the row as driver or corroboration.
queue_items.proposed_change: In strongest_rejected_alternative, ground the discriminator in the far-side bytes (the verse-initial ה֣וֹי at oshb:Isa.1.4, token 1, byte tier) and state why the accent_stripped-tier plural-noun catchword is a hinge rather than continuity; span unchanged.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with the double imperative-vocative summons שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ (oshb:Isa.1.2, byte tier), “Hear, heavens, and listen, earth; for Yahweh has spoken” (web:Isa.1.2), calling cosmic witnesses to the case before any content of the charge is stated; verse 3's ox/donkey analogy completes the witness-testimony frame (“The ox knows his owner… but Israel doesn't know”, web:Isa.1.3). The row closes before the hoy-onset indictment proper begins at web:Isa.1.4.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this witness-summons couplet into the following indictment as one unbroken oracle was rejected because the couplet opens with the witness-summons imperatives שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ (oshb:Isa.1.2, tokens 1-4, byte tier) and the rebellion charge follows within the same verse, making this a summons-plus-indictment preface rather than an offense-free one, a distinct move from the hoy-onset indictment that follows.
shipped_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
shipped_row.device_notes: The heaven/earth witness-pair convention is a recognized covenant-lawsuit opening move argued here from the imperative pairing itself, not from a named riv/din verb (contrast the explicit riv formula at 3:13). A cross-seam catchword recurs at accent_stripped tier: בָּנִים֙ (oshb:Isa.1.2, token 8) and בָּנִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.1.4, token 9) collate at accent_stripped tier, the bare plural noun standing at 8 verses book-wide (sweep: 8 verses, skeleton, token-exact).

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The row is bounded to the single chazon header verse: “The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.” (web:Isa.1.1). The Hebrew opens with חֲזוֹן֙ (oshb:Isa.1.1, byte tier), a superscription noun naming the seer, his father, and the four-king regnal window, with no imperative, vocative, or divine-speech formula of its own; the next verse opens a fresh imperative summons (“Hear, heavens, and listen, earth”, web:Isa.1.2), which is the row's own seam.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the header into the following summons unit was rejected because the header verse carries no imperative or address of its own and names a distinct royal-regnal frame absent from verse 2.
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: Both superscriptions carry the same relative clause, אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה, byte-identical at three verses book-wide — oshb:Isa.1.1, oshb:Isa.2.1, and oshb:Isa.13.1, the massa hinge (sweep: 3 verses, byte). The two superscriptions share the seer's name and the Judah/Jerusalem object; what distinguishes them is the header-noun class — חֲזוֹן֙ against הַדָּבָר֙ (oshb:Isa.1.1 / oshb:Isa.2.1, byte tier) — together with the regnal window naming Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, בִּימֵ֨י עֻזִּיָּ֧הוּ יוֹתָ֛ם אָחָ֥ז יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.1, byte tier), which has no counterpart in 2:1.

next_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with the hoy-onset indictment ה֣וֹי (oshb:Isa.1.4, byte tier), “Ah sinful nation, a people loaded with iniquity, offspring of evildoers, children who deal corruptly!” (web:Isa.1.4); this hoy functions as the opening indictment rather than a woe-oracle onset of the kind found later in the book, since it launches a description of the nation's condition rather than pronouncing doom on a named target-class. The row runs through the survivor clause “a very small remnant” (oshb:Isa.1.9) — הוֹתִ֥יר (oshb:Isa.1.9, token 4) governing שָׂרִ֖יד (token 6), a survivor verb-noun pairing outside the book's four-way remnant family — closing where a parashah setumah break falls (oshb:Isa.1.9, single-witness, tier-3) and where verse 10 opens a fresh imperative address to a new named audience.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Classifying this row as a woe_oracle of the ch-5/28-33 series type was rejected because its hoy targets the nation's condition in general description rather than pronouncing doom on a specific addressee-class, the operative distinction argued for the opening-indictment reading.
next_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
next_row.device_notes: Verse 4 carries the qadosh-Israel title קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.1.4, byte tier), “the Holy One of Israel” (web:Isa.1.4), one of the book's signature divine-title sites. A setumah break is recorded at the close of verse 9 (oshb:Isa.1.9, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only, not a boundary driver). A place-name catchword straddles the seam at hinge strength: כִּסְדֹ֣ם הָיִ֔ינוּ לַעֲמֹרָ֖ה דָּמִֽינוּ (oshb:Isa.1.9, byte tier) is picked up by קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם and עַ֥ם עֲמֹרָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.10, byte tier at each site); the Sodom and Gomorrah place-name skeletons stand at 4 and 3 verses book-wide respectively (sweep: 4 verses / 3 verses, skeleton) and co-occur in adjacent verses only here. The pair functions as a hinge across the seam — simile at 1:9, vocative address at 1:10 — rather than as argued continuity.

queue_items.claim: The stated rejection of the 1:23|1:24 rival weighs the inclusio only against the tier-3 parashah witness and never against the tier-1 divine-speech frame the row itself names as the rival's other ground.
queue_items.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative builds the rival on two grounds - the petuchah at the close of verse 23 and the neum turn at verse 24 - then rejects it because the bracket is 'a stronger, byte-grounded cohesion signal than a single tier-3 parashah witness', and device_notes adds that the rejection 'rests on the skeleton-tier inclusio bracket alone, not on the signature's position'. The neum stack is a ruled tier-1 divine-speech frame, not a tier-3 mark: נְאֻ֤ם הָֽאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת stands at tokens 2-5 of oshb:Isa.1.24 (12 tokens, byte tier re-collated, after the connective לָכֵ֗ן and ahead of אֲבִ֖יר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל at tokens 6-7), and it is left unweighed in the comparison actually stated. The row's own digits are exact on re-sweep and do support its handling: the signature stands at 23 verses book-wide (sweep: 23 verses, skeleton) and is verse-initial at exactly one site, oshb:Isa.56.8, so the 1:24 occurrence is postpositive rather than an onset; and the inclusio קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.1.21, tokens 4-5) against קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.26, tokens 12-13) collates at skeleton tier only - the meteg retained at 1:26 blocks accent_stripped - standing at 2 verses book-wide, exactly as the row names it. The mark types are right too: PE at Isa.1.23 cited as petuchah, never conflated with the SAMEKH sites at 1:20 and 1:17. The span is not shown wrong; the rejection comparison is incomplete.
queue_items.proposed_change: In strongest_rejected_alternative, weigh the rival's tier-1 component explicitly - the postpositive, non-verse-initial position of the neum signature at oshb:Isa.1.24 (token 2 of 12) against its single verse-initial site book-wide - alongside the tier-3 witness; span unchanged.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with the qinah-style exclamation אֵיכָה֙ (oshb:Isa.1.21, byte tier), “How the faithful city has become a prostitute!” (web:Isa.1.21), a fresh lament-onset distinct from the preceding conditional oracle. The unit is held together as one row by an inclusio: the two-word designation קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.1.21, byte tier) recurs at the close of verse 26, קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.26; the two sites match at skeleton tier only (sweep: 2 verses) — identical consonants, differing verse-end cantillation — so the recurrence is named at that tier and not claimed byte-identical), “the faithful city” (web:Isa.1.21) bracketing “a faithful town” (web:Isa.1.26). Between the brackets, verse 24 pivots on the stacked title-and-signature נְאֻ֤ם הָֽאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.1.24, byte tier), “Therefore the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says” (web:Isa.1.24); this hoy, ה֚וֹי, is a divine self-exclamation over Yahweh's own coming action, not a woe pronounced against the addressee, so it is read as an internal turn within the bracketed lament-to-restoration unit rather than a row-cutting seam. Verse 20, which closes just before this row opens, carries its own setumah break (oshb:Isa.1.20, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration).
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting the row at 1:23|1:24 into a separate lament (21-23) and a separate oracle (24-26) was considered, since a petuchah break is recorded at the close of verse 23 (oshb:Isa.1.23, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only) and verse 24 pivots into its own neum-formula turn at token 2 of 12, after the connective and ahead of the quoted speech; it was rejected in favor of the skeleton-tier inclusio bracket spanning 21-26, which is a stronger, byte-grounded cohesion signal than a single tier-3 parashah witness, and the rejection rests on that bracket alone.
shipped_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
shipped_row.device_notes: Held at medium_low because the unity argument (the inclusio) and the tier-3 division signal (the petuchah at 1:23) genuinely pull in opposite directions; this is disclosed rather than silently resolved. The neum stack at 1:24, נְאֻ֤ם הָֽאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.1.24, byte tier), stands at token 2 of 12 — after the discourse connective לָכֵ֗ן and ahead of the quoted speech it introduces — and across the 23-verse book-wide census of the signature (sweep: 23 verses, skeleton) it is verse-initial only at oshb:Isa.56.8; the rejection of the 1:23|1:24 rival rests on the skeleton-tier inclusio bracket alone, not on the signature's position. A chapter-level lexical bracket, not cross-seam cohesion at 1:17|1:18: the orphan clause inverts word order across the two sites — verb-noun at שִׁפְט֣וּ יָת֔וֹם (oshb:Isa.1.17) to noun-verb at יָתוֹם֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁפֹּ֔טוּ (oshb:Isa.1.23) — while the widow member, imperative-plus-noun at רִ֖יבוּ אַלְמָנָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.17), recurs as the construct noun phrase וְרִ֥יב אַלְמָנָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.1.23); the orphan noun matching at accent_stripped tier and the widow noun at skeleton tier across the two sites, the orphan noun standing at 2 verses and the widow noun at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses / 3 verses, skeleton, token-exact).

prev_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with the divine invitation formula לְכוּ נָ֛א וְנִוָּֽכְחָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.1.18, byte tier), “Come now, and let's reason together,” says Yahweh (web:Isa.1.18), a distinct speech-act (invitation to settlement) from the imperative catalogue that precedes it. The row runs through the closing formula כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר (oshb:Isa.1.20, byte tier), “for Yahweh's mouth has spoken it.” (oshb:Isa.1.20), a recognized oracle-closing signature that recurs byte-identically at 3 verses book-wide, also at oshb:Isa.40.5 (כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר) and oshb:Isa.58.14 (כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר) (sweep: 3 verses, byte), all three carrying the ki-form, where a setumah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.1.20, single-witness, tier-3). This same opening seam has its own tier-3 witness too: a setumah break closes verse 17 (oshb:Isa.1.17, single-witness) immediately before the row begins.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching verses 18-20 to the preceding ritual-critique unit as its conclusion was rejected because verse 18 opens with its own imperative-plus-cohortative invitation, לְכוּ נָ֛א וְנִוָּֽכְחָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.1.18, tokens 1-3, byte tier), a fresh speech-act distinct from the imperative catalogue of verses 16-17; the quotative יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה that follows at tokens 4-5 is not itself a discriminator, since it recurs mid-verse inside that same catalogue's block at oshb:Isa.1.11 (יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה, accent_stripped tier; the bare quotative stands at 5 verses book-wide, sweep: 5 verses, skeleton, distinct from the 5 vav-prefixed narrative-onset sites).

prev_row.device_notes: The unit is conditional in structure (willing-and-obedient vs. refuse-and-rebel), which argues for judgment_oracle over salvation_oracle since the promise is contingent rather than unconditional comfort.

next_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with צִיּ֖וֹן בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט תִּפָּדֶ֑ה (oshb:Isa.1.27, byte tier), “Zion shall be redeemed with justice, and her converts with righteousness.” (web:Isa.1.27), shifting from the first-person ‘I will’ divine speech of 1:24-26 to third-person declarative summary naming Zion's redeemed and the apostates' fate side by side, a discourse-mode shift read as the row's opening seam. The row closes the chapter at וְהָיָ֤ה הֶחָסֹן֙ לִנְעֹ֔רֶת וּפֹעֲל֖וֹ לְנִיצ֑וֹץ וּבָעֲר֧וּ (oshb:Isa.1.31, byte tier), “The strong will be like tinder, and his work like a spark. They will both burn” (oshb:Isa.1.31), where a setumah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.1.31, single-witness, tier-3), and before the fresh ha-davar superscription opening chapter 2.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 1:21-31 as one unbounded row was rejected because verse 27 drops the first-person divine voice of the neum-framed oracle for a third-person summary, and holding 27-31 as a separate closing statement lets the 21-26 inclusio stand as its own bracketed unit; the 26|27 seam itself is argued from this mode shift alone, with no explicit lexical frame marker, so it is held at reduced confidence.

next_row.device_notes: The oak/garden withering imagery of verses 29-30 anticipates the fire imagery closing verse 31, forming the chapter's own closing figure rather than a list register; no separate row is cut for it. An adjacent-verse righteousness-root catchword straddles the row's own opening seam: הַצֶּ֔דֶק (oshb:Isa.1.26, token 11) is picked up by בִּצְדָקָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.27, token 5), byte tier at each site, in consecutive verses, a catchword straddling this row's own front seam at 1:26|1:27. A chapter-level bracket rides behind it: the justice/righteousness co-occurrence object stands at 16 verses book-wide and at exactly 2 verses in this chapter, oshb:Isa.1.21 and oshb:Isa.1.27 (sweep: 16 verses / 2 verses, skeleton); at oshb:Isa.1.27 the form is בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט (token 2), prefixed, not the bare noun מִשְׁפָּ֗ט of oshb:Isa.1.21 (token 7).

queue_items.claim: The row's only opening-seam driver is a Hebrew form-class claim - a first-person to third-person discourse-mode shift - argued with no pointed splice of the verb forms it rests on.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale rests the 1:26|1:27 seam on the shift from the first-person divine speech of 1:24-26 to third-person declarative summary, and strongest_rejected_alternative concedes the seam 'is argued from this mode shift alone, with no explicit lexical frame marker'. The claim is byte-true - oshb:Isa.1.26 opens וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה (token 1 of 13) and the verb of oshb:Isa.1.27 is תִּפָּדֶ֑ה (token 3 of 5) - but neither form is spliced anywhere in the row: the seam's label is carried by an English rendering, while the only pointed evidence the row offers at this seam is the righteousness catchword, which it correctly reports as straddling the seam, that is, as material pulling the other way. Campaign law makes the pointed splice with its tier mandatory for a boundary-relevant original-language claim, and form-class labels carry the same discipline as digits. Confidence is held at medium_low with the frontier flag set, which is the calibrated handling for a mode-shift-only seam, so the seam is under-evidenced in the row rather than shown wrong, and no tier-4 signal is used as driver or corroboration anywhere in the row.
queue_items.proposed_change: Splice the two verb forms at byte tier into boundary_rationale - וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה (oshb:Isa.1.26, token 1) against תִּפָּדֶ֑ה (oshb:Isa.1.27, token 3) - as the pointed ground of the person shift; span unchanged.
